strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the reopened local Runtime platform/deadline/durability blocker by making MCP stdio deadlines absolute across response and child-exit waits and by proving durable write failure behavior under deterministic failpoints.
Keeps task terminal status mutation, cancellation freshness, MCP timeout classification, and process cleanup evidence inside Rust Runtime/store authority.
Preserves controlled MCP stdio execution while preventing late child exits and late task completions from escaping bounded Runtime deadline and terminal-state checks.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by closing the reopened local Runtime platform/deadline/durability blocker with concrete deadline, race, and durable write failure evidence.
answers.new_capability: MCP stdio requests now share one absolute RuntimeDeadline across response wait and child-exit wait, terminal task updates can require status plus updated_at freshness, and durable writes have deterministic failpoints proving fail-closed behavior for disk-full, truncated-temp, and rename-denial cases.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-7 covered task-state atomic writes and existing timeout cleanup tokens, but review found missing evidence for deadline budget reset after response, late child exit cleanup, timeout/cancel/tool-response races, and durable failure injection.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A Runtime subprocess could answer and then linger beyond the intended timeout budget, a late completion could overwrite a concurrent cancel, and durable failure cases would remain unproven before release.
answers.non_duplicative: This is the RRP-7.1 corrective for deadline, cross-platform boundary, and failure-injection evidence; it is not durable schema migration, MCP approval retry safety, protocol/event semantic contracts, module decomposition, or direct CI workflow hardening.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-7.1 adds no JSON-RPC method and preserves existing Runtime protocol, CLI, VSIX, MCP, replay, ledger, and Product DoD surfaces.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The updated artifacts are release-readiness assessment and guard evidence, not runtime diagnostic endpoints, report wrappers, dashboards, or user-facing summary features.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: MCP stdio response handling now waits for child exit only within the original absolute timeout budget before process-tree cleanup; terminal task completion/cancel paths can reject stale state; test-only durable write failpoints prove fail-closed behavior without changing production APIs beyond the checked store mutation helper.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless controllers get stronger local Runtime guarantees that stdio subprocesses cannot extend timeout budget after answering, terminal task races fail closed, and durable write failures do not silently replace or corrupt task state.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the reopened P1 platform-deadline-durability-hardening blocker while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until RRP-5.1, runtime-release-guard-ci, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: RuntimeDeadline carries an absolute expiration instant and stdio_request uses deadline.remaining_or_zero() for response wait plus wait_for_stdio_child_exit_or_timeout for post-response child exit.

MCP stdio late-exit tests launch a real child process that writes a valid response and then sleeps; Runtime kills it when the original timeout budget expires and reports bounded process-tree cleanup evidence.
TaskStore::update_task_status_with_payload_checked rereads task state and rejects status or updated_at drift before terminal completion/cancel evidence can overwrite a concurrent state transition.

Test-only thread-local durable write failpoint cases cover disk_full_before_write, truncated_state_before_rename, and rename_denied_after_sync while asserting no committed state replacement, no terminal ledger append, and no temporary-file leakage.
The phase does not set runtime_release_ready=true, change license/publish/release metadata, start hosted platform work, or modify .github workflow files.

guard:platform-deadline-durability stops requiring the new RRP-7.1 implementation and test evidence
hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote Git expansion, signing, release assets, or external platform products are added

CLI, VSIX, external controller state, prose, model output, raw prompts, provider output, file contents, paths, secrets, environment values, executable content, or process output are treated as Runtime authority

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-7.1 changes guard-engine files, the current phase manifest, and Runtime release-readiness audit while closing the reopened platform-deadline-durability-hardening blocker. Review must confirm the absolute RuntimeDeadline budget spans response and child-exit waits, late child exits are killed with bounded evidence, terminal task races fail closed, durable write failure injection proves disk-full/truncated-temp/rename-denial behavior, guard negative tests fail closed, and Runtime Release Ready remains false.

exit_criteria: MCP stdio response wait and child-exit wait share one absolute RuntimeDeadline budget.
Late child exit after a valid stdio response is bounded by the same timeout and produces process-tree cleanup evidence.
Task terminal completion/cancel paths can fail closed when expected status or updated_at freshness no longer matches.
Durable write failpoints cover disk-full-before-write, truncated-temp-before-rename, and rename-denied-after-sync behavior without committed-state replacement or temp leakage.
guard:platform-deadline-durability fails when RRP-7.1 deadline, failure-injection, checked-terminal-race, or runtime_release_ready evidence is removed.
Runtime Release Ready remains false and runtime-release-guard-ci plus RRP-5.1 remain open.
behavior_evidence: pnpm guard:platform-deadline-durability validates RRP-7.1 source-level evidence.
pnpm guard:platform-deadline-durability:test covers deadline, late-exit, durable failpoint, checked terminal update, and runtime_release_ready negative cases.

accepted_capability: MCP stdio uses an absolute Runtime deadline across response and child-exit waits.
Late child exits after a response are killed within the original timeout budget with bounded evidence.
Terminal task state races can fail closed before stale completion/cancel overwrite.
Durable write failure injection proves fail-closed behavior for disk-full, truncated-temp, and rename-denial cases.
behavior_evidence: Focused brownie-runtime tests cover RuntimeDeadline reconstruction and real late-child-exit cleanup.
Focused brownie-store tests cover durable write failpoints and stale terminal status rejection.
guard:platform-deadline-durability and its tests enforce RRP-7.1 evidence through the existing VSIX check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime/store remain execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-7.1 closes the reopened local Runtime platform/deadline/durability blocker with concrete deadline, race, and durable write failure evidence.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until RRP-5.1, the remaining Runtime CI blocker, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; existing Runtime JSON-RPC and ledger semantics are preserved.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-7.1.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-7.1.
